UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                             BEFORE THE
               FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


Southwest Power Pool Market Monitoring Unit                    Docket No. ER26-247-000


         COMMENTS OF THE SOUTHWEST POWER POOL MARKET
                       MONITORING UNIT
The Southwest Power Pool Market Monitoring Unit (SPP MMU) respectfully submits
these comments1 in support of Southwest Power Pool (SPP)’s proposed modifications to
its Open Access Transmission Tariff (Tariff Modifications), including the additions of
Attachment BA (HILLS) and Attachment BB (HILLGA) as described in SPP’s transmittal
letter, when considering the policy in light of the current paradigm.

    I.     Introduction

SPP is facing an unprecedented number of requests to interconnect High Impact Large
Loads (HILLs).2 HILLs “pose unique challenges to the continued reliable and economic
operation of the bulk electric transmission system.”3 But HILLs also present “significant
economic and national security opportunities.”4 On June 30, 2025, SPP submitted Revision
Request 696 (RR696) to SPP’s Tariff. RR696, in part, addressed concerns with the increase
in HILL developments throughout SPP’s jurisdiction.

The SPP MMU recognizes the potential for disruption of market efficiency and equity with
any rapid change to market structure, but that the urgency associated with having an
undefined process for HILLs required SPP to move quicker than usual. As a result, the
SPP MMU has been an active participant in the revision process, engaging with RR696
and other HILL-related issues, culminating in extensive, but focused, comments in the
stakeholder process.5


1
  The MMU’s proper role in the SPP stakeholder process is advisory, not decisional. The MMU
has no decision-making role in the ultimate resolution of this matter in any SPP forum, at the
SPP Board, or at FERC. See Wholesale Competition in Regions with Organized Electric Markets,
Order No. 719, 73 Fed. Reg. 64,100 (Oct. 28, 2008), FERC Stats. & Regs. ¶ 31,281 (2008); 18
C.F.R. § 35.28(g)(3)(ii) (2024); SPP OATT Attachment AG, § 1.3.

    II.     Comments on RR696 as applicable to this and future filings
Adequate oversight of Market Participants by SPP and the SPP MMU

The revisions to the SPP Tariff set out new requirements for market participants connecting
HILLs. For example, adhering to the integrated marketplace rules (Attachment BA, § 2.2.2;
Attachment AE, § 2.22), ride-through capability (Attachment BA § 2.2.5), and installing
phasor measurement units (PMUs) or similar equipment (Attachment BA § 2.2.4). To
ensure adequate oversight of requirements like these, the SPP MMU proposed insertion of
language regarding requirements for the accuracy of data and information submitted, and
modified versions appear in Attachment BA § 2.3 and Attachment BB § 13.8. The SPP
MMU supports the inclusion of this language to effectuate adequate oversight of the
proposed processes.

Ensure that SPP’s planning process considers known limitations on generation

To ensure that generation required to meet new (and existing) loads in the SPP footprint,
the SPP MMU recommended that SPP commit to ensuring engineering and planning
processes account for run-time-limited resources. The SPP MMU made this
recommendation in the 2023 Annual State of the Market (ASOM) as part of
recommendation 2023-2. For example, in certain cases, generation may not be available
continuously due to known regulatory, environmental, or other operational reasons. The
SPP MMU generally supports the incremental progress that SPP has made on this issue in
the current filing. See Transmittal Letter at 44 (citing Proposed Tariff, Attachment AX,
Addendum 1 (“Details of planned Generation: vi[.] Any expected environmental
restrictions (e.g., run-time restrictions) or any other restrictions or limitations.”)). The SPP
MMU continues to encourage continued development in this area as the HILL process
evolves and expands to include other initiatives on SPP’s roadmap.

Address the lack of incentives for HILL load forecast accuracy

In the overall development of this proposal, the SPP MMU was concerned that HILLs,
whether deemed conforming or non-conforming load, were not incentivized to submit
accurate operational load forecasts. An increase in large loads on the system will only
increase the current operational needs for accurate load forecasts to be used in the
Reliability Unit Commitment process. This will become critical the more HILLs
interconnect, and inaccurate operational forecasts will result in inefficient commitment of
generation and improper make-whole payment allocation. SPP should pursue future tariff
changes that will address this incentive issue.




                                               2
 Other Items:
          Grandfathering

As a guiding principle, requirements for HILLs should either immediately apply to all load
meeting the criterion; or there should be a reasonable near-term line-of-sight to applying
the requirements to existing HILLs. The SPP MMU encourages SPP to re-evaluate the
grandfathering of HILL requirements following implementation.

          Demand Response

HILLs will be eligible to participate in the SPP market as Demand Response (DR). SPP is
currently bringing tariff revisions related to DR through the stakeholder process, and the
SPP MMU is continuing to engage with SPP and stakeholders to improve DR rules in the
tariff. As assets in SPP’s footprint continue to be maximized and stretched, it is of the
utmost importance for SPP to improve its DR framework to ensure it is fundamentally
sound.

      III.    Summary of the SPP MMU position on this docket

Overall, the SPP MMU agrees that HILLs are unique. They have unique operational
characteristics (including non-conforming load profiles, rapid ramp rates and flutter, and
power quality sensitivities which are magnified due to their single site location), reliability
impacts, and generator interconnection and availability pressures.6 And, these loads are
already requesting and proceeding with interconnection to the SPP Transmission System
without recognition or definition of their specific characteristics.7 SPP has expressed, and
the SPP MMU supports, the need to provide tools and frameworks to begin analyzing these
unique loads as they interconnect to the SPP Transmission System on a consistent basis.

The SPP MMU still has concerns generally with how HILLs will be integrated into the
grid, and this proposal is not perfect as discussed in our comments in the SPP stakeholder
process. Nevertheless, after weighing all of the above, the SPP MMU agrees the
Commission should accept this tariff filing as the first step to a stronger large load policy
framework at SPP.

                                                   Respectfully submitted,

                                                   /s/Carrie Bivens
                                                   Carrie Bivens,
                                                     Vice President, Market Monitoring
